clue.text: Bar gadabout in oriental Jew's coat

indicators.note: the run-together word gadabout is read as gad about, so the gad letters go around the bar

parts.note: to gad is to roam idly; taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
E for East, the oriental direction

explanation.surface: Someone at a bar, a gadabout, wears a long coat in Eastern style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gadabout' must be split into GAD plus 'about', the container signal: GAD around BAR gives GABARD, then IN and E. The long coat was traditionally worn by Jews in medieval times.
explanation.definitionFit: The gabardine was the loose long cloak associated with medieval Jewish dress, as in Shylock's 'Jewish gaberdine'.

clue.text: Relish university getting stumped in a game

indicators.note: the university and stumped letters go within the game

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game
st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A student is out in a cricket match but enjoys it all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is zest or enjoyment, the same as relish.

clue.text: King at centre of noisy, disapproval for engagement

indicators.note: the king goes into the middle of the disapproving word

parts.note: booing is noisy disapproval
K for king in chess

explanation.surface: A king is booed at his engagement ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A booking is an engagement, as of a performer for a show.

clue.text: Remember to note reversed charge

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
a collect call is one charged to the receiver

explanation.surface: A reminder to note that a phone charge was reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect call is the US name for a reverse-charge call, paid for by the person called.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to recall or bring back to memory.

clue.text: I am to some extent fairly exposed

parts.note: contracted to I'm
partially means to some extent

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being somewhat exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' is a link flourish: read the answer split as I'M PARTIALLY and it says 'I am to some extent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting impartially means acting without bias, which is acting fairly.

clue.text: Make last thousand in notes

indicators.note: the thousand letter sits within the two notes

parts.note: E is a musical note, here twice

explanation.surface: Stretch a thousand pounds' worth of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests banknotes; it is two musical notes, E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To eke out supplies is to make them last longer.

clue.text: Support for an airman in command

indicators.note: the airman's letters sit within the word for command

parts.note: to bid is to command or order
PO is Pilot Officer, an RAF rank

explanation.surface: Backing given to a pilot who has been put in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-legged stand, as under a rifle or camera, is a kind of support.

clue.text: Base-sounding comic

parts.note: base sounds like bass, so a comic singer with a bass voice in Italian opera

explanation.definitionFit: In opera this is a comic role, typically sung by a bass, as in basso buffo.

clue.text: Napier's perfect confession

parts.note: the Latin perfect tense for 'I have sinned', reputedly the general's punning message on taking Sind in 1843

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Charles Napier supposedly reported his capture of Sind with one Latin word meaning 'I have sinned'; 'perfect' is the tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin perfect-tense verb means 'I have sinned', an admission of guilt.

clue.text: Caught sight of rescinded order

indicators.note: the letters of rescinded are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone noticed that an order had been cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like the thing rescinded, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern something is to perceive or make it out with the eyes.

clue.text: Writer to select for summit coverage

parts.note: C. P. Snow, the English novelist
to cap a player is to select them for a national team

explanation.surface: A writer is chosen to report on a top-level political meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summit coverage' suggests press reports of a summit meeting; here it is literal, what covers a mountain top. To CAP a sportsperson is the British usage for picking them for a national side.
explanation.definitionFit: The layer of white on a mountain peak literally covers the summit.

clue.text: Results of property

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both consequences and one's movable goods or belongings.

clue.text: Oiler wrecked in the bay

indicators.note: the letters of oiler are smashed up and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An oil tanker runs aground and breaks up in the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like a stretch of coast for the wrecked tanker, but it is an architectural bay window.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a projecting upper-floor window, a type of bay window.

clue.text: Engineers go on about outside broadcast being abandoned

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: the word for going on wraps around the broadcast abbreviation

parts.note: to prate is to go on, talk at tedious length

explanation.surface: Army engineers grumble that an outside broadcast has been dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned here means morally depraved, the sense of a reprobate as an unprincipled person.

clue.text: Spanish King with two queens? A ladies' man, obviously!

parts.note: Phil, short for Philip, the name of several kings of Spain
and means with

indicators.note: the queen letters appear twice in a row

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A Spanish monarch with two queens is plainly a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: Philip II of Spain married four times; ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A philanderer is a man who flirts or has affairs with many women.

clue.text: Weed got from a bundle of sticks

indicators.note: got is taken away from the bundle word

parts.note: a faggot is a bundle of sticks for firewood
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weed is found growing in a bundle of firewood sticks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' is slang for tobacco, and FAG is British slang for a cigarette; FAGGOT less GOT leaves it.
explanation.definitionFit: Weed is slang for tobacco, and a fag is British slang for a cigarette.

clue.text: Selling rights are his in a foreign country

indicators.note: his goes within the country

parts.note: France, foreign to a British solver
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's commercial rights lie abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a licence granted to sell a company's goods or services.

clue.text: Backward race, leading one country into liquidation

indicators.note: the turned race comes in front of what follows
the race word is read from end to start

parts.note: the mile is a classic race distance
the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A country lags in a race and leads its people into financial ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns MILE into ELIM, and 'leading' puts it before I and NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquidation means wiping out or getting rid of, as elimination does.

clue.text: Eccentric lad goes in next door

indicators.note: the letters of lad goes in behave oddly and rearrange

explanation.surface: An odd young man moves into the house next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means beside or adjacent, as a neighbour next door is.

clue.text: A loan I'm told, negotiated in a schooner, perhaps

indicators.note: a loan is negotiated, and so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone says a loan was arranged aboard a sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schooner' suggests a ship; it is also a large sherry glass, and amontillado is a sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a tall sherry glass, and this medium-dry Spanish sherry is what may be served in it.

clue.text: One boss to unsettle windy players

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boss sets out to unnerve the nervous members of the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windy' suggests nervous, but it means playing wind instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboe players play a wind instrument, so they are windy players.

clue.text: Some sheets to sleep in here?

definitions.meaning: slang for a bed or one's flat

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a writing block of paper and slang for a place to sleep or live.

clue.text: Character sketch taking a sideways look

definitions.meaning: a short written portrait of a person
an outline of a face seen from the side

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a short biographical article and a side view of a face.

clue.text: Ill-humoured, I'd say, and visually impaired

parts.note: cross means angry or bad-tempered

indicators.note: the word I'd is spoken, and its sound is spelt another way

parts.note: pronounced like 'eyed'

explanation.surface: A grumpy person admits to poor eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'd say' looks like a speaker's hedge; 'say' is the sound signal on I'd.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a squint, with eyes turned inwards, is a visual impairment.

clue.text: Sensational photo inside 'the ..borders of Surrey

indicators.note: the photo word goes within the county's outside letters
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: pic is short for picture or photo

explanation.surface: A scandalous photo is taken inside the county of Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south of London; its first and last letters S and Y enclose PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicy means racy or scandalous, as sensational stories are.

clue.text: Clean servant

definitions.meaning: to brush and tidy, as of a horse
a stable hand who looks after horses

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for brushing and tidying an animal and a stable servant.

clue.text: Strength of will possibly

definitions.meaning: the modal verb of possibility, softer than will

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for power and the modal verb expressing what perhaps will happen.

clue.text: Introduce gradually, even in the beginning

indicators.note: the small word in is placed at the start

parts.note: taken as written
still means even, as in 'even better' or 'still better'

explanation.surface: Bring something in slowly, and do so right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the beginning' reads as one phrase, but IN is a piece and 'the beginning' puts it before STILL.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea or habit is to impart it gradually; INSTILL is the US spelling.

clue.text: Old mead, pound per head

parts.note: L for pound, from Latin libra
ea is short for each

explanation.surface: An ancient honey drink costs a pound a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mead' suggests the honey drink; it is the poetic word for meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is a poetic or archaic word for a meadow or grassland, as mead is too.

clue.text: Call outside help for making foray

indicators.note: the call word goes around the help word

parts.note: to ring is to phone, call
aid is help

explanation.surface: A phone call asks for back-up before a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a raid, so making one is raiding.

clue.text: Attempt classical art, for example

parts.note: es is Latin for 'thou art'
say means for example

explanation.surface: Try classical art, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classical art' suggests Greek sculpture; it is the Latin verb form es, 'thou art'.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it, and an essay is an attempt.

clue.text: Similar cases in this settlement

definitions.meaning: in grammar, words matching in case, number or gender
a deal or accord reached between parties

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both grammatical concord, as nouns and adjectives matching case, and a negotiated deal.
